title: Canada advances to CONCACAF Nations League semifinals with win over Guatemala
summary: The Canadian men's soccer team closed out its 2026 schedule in style on Monday night with an emphatic 4-1 victory over Guatemala to secure a berth in the final four of the CONCACAF Nations League.

blocks.text: Soccer
The Canadian men's soccer team closed out its 2026 schedule in style on Monday night with an emphatic 4-1 victory over Guatemala to secure a berth in the final four of the CONCACAF Nations League.
Tani Oluwaseyi scored twice in 4-1 victory, Canada advances 7-3 on aggregate
Oluwaseyi scores twice to lift Canada to CONCACAF Nations League semifinals
Tani Oluwaseyi scored twice for the host side, which got singles from Jonathan David and Tajon Buchanan in the 7-3 aggregate victory.
"This game today, we dominated from start to finish in all facets of the game," Oluwaseyi said. "On the ball, off the ball and all the different parts of the field."
Canada had 68 per cent of possession and had nine shots on target. Oscar Santis scored on Guatemala's lone shot on goal.
Canada earned a 3-2 win in the opening leg last Friday at Guatemala City but lost captain Alphonso Davies to a lower-body injury.

Canada will move on to the CONCACAF Nations League Finals in Los Angeles in March 2027 and also qualified for the 2027 Gold Cup. Guatemala has to settle for an appearance in the Gold Cup preliminary round.

blocks.text: The two-game series provided the Canadian team its first competitive matches since reaching the Round of 16 at the FIFA World Cup last summer. It was the first time Canada had reached the knockout stage at the tournament.
David wore the captain's armband in the return match on a clear, chilly night at BMO Field. Assistant Mauro Biello filled in as head coach after Jesse Marsch's red card in the opener.
"We put our principles in place and players come in and the team doesn't skip a beat," Biello said. "That's what it's about."
Canada controlled play for most of the opening half but had some difficulty burying chances.
Liam Millar was denied on a brilliant save by goalkeeper Kenderson Navarro in the 27th minute and Luc De Fougerolles was stoned in front moments later.
A botched clearing attempt led to Guatemala's goal in the 34th minute. De Fougerolles' clearance hit teammate Niko Sigur and bounced in front to Santis, who pivoted and slotted it home.
David answered from the penalty spot in the 39th minute after he was tripped up near the goal. Navarro guessed with a dive to his left as David powered a shot high to the opposite side.
"We call him the Iceman for a reason," Biello said. "He took that moment and he was able to rally the team after that."
Oluwaseyi gave Canada the lead in the first minute of stoppage time. The host side didn't let up after the halftime break as Buchanan tallied in the 53rd minute.
"We all believed that we were going to finish our chances off and I think we did that in the end," Buchanan said.

David orchestrated a pretty passing play in the 62nd minute as Canada pulled away. He delivered a cross to Millar, who headed the ball across the six-yard box to Oluwaseyi, who headed it home for the brace.
In the opening leg, David, Millar and Oluwaseyi scored the Canada goals. Guatemala tallied early in the second half and made it a one-goal game on a late Canadian own goal.

blocks.text: Davies, who suffered a minor muscle strain in the opener, made his first start with the national team since tearing a knee ligament in March 2025, a period of more than 600 days.
A hamstring injury limited to him just one game appearance at the World Cup. The Bayern Munich star returned to Germany for treatment over the weekend.
Davies missed Canada's fall friendlies against Chile in Toronto, Peru in Montreal and the United States in Minnesota while on his honeymoon.
He joined a long injury list for the Canadian side that includes Jonathan Osorio, Jacob Shaffelburg, Stephen Eustáquio, Cyle Larin, Derek Cornelius, Alfie Jones and Alistair Johnston.
Former Canadian men's captain Julian de Guzman was honoured at halftime. He earned 89 caps for the national team.
